corpus.note: Passwords are generated, never stored. Rows are keyed by sample_id; regenerating from the same seed reproduces the corpus exactly.

frequency_source.semantics: Zipf frequency: log10(occurrences per billion tokens) of the NATIVE-SCRIPT word in a general text corpus. A corpus word frequency -- not a password frequency and not a model score.
frequency_source.license: Apache-2.0 (package); aggregated corpora under their own terms
frequency_source.notes: wordfreq 3.x is a frozen dataset: its author stopped updating it in 2024, which makes it reproducible but means it reflects pre-2022 text. Only a 'small' list ships for Hindi (~27k words).

word_distribution.note: Unobserved entries are bounded by the smallest OBSERVED probability and scaled by their tier's measured frequency coverage. No frequency is invented for them, and frequency stays null on the entry itself.

structure_prior.form: truncated geometric over segment count, renormalised
structure_prior.status: assumption -- no password corpus exists in this repository

question: Does a probabilistic grammar over Romanized-Indic password structure carry information a generic estimator lacks, without inventing structure in strings that have none?

character_model.note: Cost is -log10 P per character; lower means the model finds the text likelier. The dictionary-present and dictionary-absent rows are the generalisation test: if they match, the model learned the shape of the language rather than its vocabulary. The floor row is the bar any of it has to clear before it can change a reported estimate.

random_control.note: word_rate is how often the winning derivation contains a dictionary segment; below_bruteforce_rate is how often the grammar alone priced a random string below enumerating it. The second is the one that could change an estimate. A model that read random strings as cheaper than brute force would be inventing structure, and every Indic result would have to be read as the same artefact.

ablations.name: no_bruteforce_floor
ablations.description: The grammar's own number, with min(grammar, brute force) turned off. Isolates what the retained non-PCFG floor is doing -- on the random controls, everything.

ablations.name: no_character_model
ablations.description: The `unknown` category removed, so only dictionary words, digits, years and symbols can derive a span. This is the PCFG WITHOUT the character n-gram: it isolates the component added to address Milestone 2's coverage ceiling.

ablations.name: no_dictionary
ablations.description: The `word` category removed. Everything alphabetic must go through the character model. Isolates the lexicon from the shape model -- the two halves of the Indic claim.

ablations.name: segments_0.3
ablations.description: Structure prior with q=0.3 instead of 0.5: multi-segment passwords are assumed rarer. An ASSUMPTION arm -- no data chose 0.5 either.

ablations.name: segments_0.7
ablations.description: Structure prior with q=0.7: multi-segment passwords assumed commoner. The other side of the same assumption.

ablations.name: category_lexical
ablations.description: Category prior skewed towards lexical segments (word 0.40, unknown 0.30, digits 0.15, symbols 0.10, year 0.05) instead of uniform. Plausible, and measured by nothing -- which is exactly why it is an arm and not the default. It bounds what the maximum-entropy choice costs.

ablations.name: curve_seed_7
ablations.description: The same grammar with the guess curve re-sampled from a different seed. Not a design choice: this bounds the Monte-Carlo estimator's own variance, so a reader can tell a real effect from sampling noise.

ablations.name: ngram_order_3
ablations.description: A shorter character model. Less context, more backoff.

ablations.name: ngram_order_5
ablations.description: A longer character model. More context, sparser counts.

ablations.name: ngram_curated_only
ablations.description: The character model trained without the 120,000-entry mined tier, which is the least precise source and the one Milestone 2 had to clear of carrying its result.

ablations.name: unranked_uniform
ablations.description: Entries with no observed frequency weighted alike across tiers instead of by their tier's measured coverage.

ablations.name: unranked_excluded
ablations.description: Entries with no observed frequency dropped from the word category entirely -- 86% of the dictionary -- leaving the character model to explain them.

interpretation_note: A lower estimate is NOT automatically a more accurate one. Establishing that needs a reference attack -- a cracking run against a real leak -- which this project does not have. These numbers state the direction and the magnitude and stop there.
